text:
Erik Cernak has nine assists and no goals in 20 games, and eight of those assists came in his last ten. For a defenseman whose job is hits, blocks and the penalty kill, that's an unusual run, and our numbers credit most of it to his teammates' finishing. We'd expect about 3.2 points at his ice time over that stretch, and the chances with him on the ice are up only a little (8.8 on-ice expected goals against 8.3 usual).

The underlying play is good, though. At five on five Tampa Bay takes 61.6% of the expected goals with him on, 6.8 points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him taking chances away last season (86th percentile), with penalties the one cost (2.5 goals).

He missed time in mid-November and returned on Nov. 17 along with Anthony Cirelli and Brayden Point, per The Hockey News, then played 22 minutes against Edmonton two nights later. The 6'4" two-time Stanley Cup winner has 34 hits and 31 blocks. Our numbers expect the assist pace to slow; the role is the constant.
